sources.entry: TaskExplorer - Explore all processes running on your Mac with TaskExplorer. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/objective-see/TaskExplorer)

summary.name: TaskExplorer
summary.one_liner: A macOS process explorer from Objective-See that live-lists every running process with its code signing status, loaded dylibs, open files, and network connections, plus an optional built-in AI assistant.
use_cases: Investigating which processes are listening on the network
Finding ad-hoc or unsigned processes running on a Mac
Checking which processes load a given dylib
Scanning running processes for VirusTotal-flagged malware
Exporting a snapshot of running processes and connections as JSON
summary.what_it_does: TaskExplorer shows every running process live, updating as processes start and exit, with its icon, path, pid, user, and code signing status (Apple, Developer ID, ad-hoc, or unsigned). For a selected process it lists loaded dylibs, open files, or network connections, and an inspector pane gives hashes, signing details, and parent/child relationships. A filter field supports keyword tokens such as #3rdparty, #adhoc, #network, #listening, #root, and #everything for searching across dylibs, files, and connections. An optional AI assistant answers questions about the live data, and a command-line mode outputs JSON.
notable: Built on Apple's Endpoint Security framework, with a system extension for live process monitoring
Built-in AI assistant that runs on-device via Apple Intelligence or uses the user's own Claude or ChatGPT API key
Optional VirusTotal integration that flags known-malicious processes and dylibs in red, sending only file hashes
Command-line mode outputs JSON for scripting, and the app can export all data as JSON
caveats: Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer; the on-device assistant needs macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence on Apple silicon, and older systems need a Claude or ChatGPT key
Needs System Settings approval for the system extension and Full Disk Access before it can monitor processes
Version 2.1.0 is the option for macOS 11 to 13
